cells.tense: The choosing is happening here, with your hand on the pen.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: When someone near you can't hold their own course for a while, carry part of it for them until they can.
cells.core:
You can pick a direction and not defend it at the same time, and that's rare. There's a course you know is right before you know why, and you carry it lightly — no case to argue, nobody to convince. It holds. When someone close to you is unclear about theirs, you can lend a hand without taking over.

It travels, this way you have, so give it to one person this week while they wobble. No pitch, no selling the road you took. Just be the weight on their side until they can stand. You don't have to produce a reason for them. What you're carrying is already enough to lean on.
cells.sheetLine: You know the course you're on, and you don't force it.
cells.verb: to pick the light to steer by and steer by it
cells.place: where you know what matters before you know why

cells.tense: You will already be bracing for what can't be written in yet.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Sit with the tugs running through you — several at once, all loud — and go through them one by one until you can tell which began with you.
cells.core:
You're choosing with such force that every option has started to feel like forever. Which calling to follow is already being settled somewhere years out, and the answer arrives before anything happens. The direction gets picked, then defended hard, because what's chosen now has to hold for all the time afterward.

Take the tugs apart instead. Several pull on you at once and each one claims to be the one, so go through them one at a time until you can tell which began with you and which got picked up along the way. The crossing will loosen once you stop staring through it. What you're really after is smaller than the decision.
cells.sheetLine: You've turned one pick into a ruling that has to last forever.

cells.tense: You kept the harvest, and you're still at the door you first entered.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Choose one finished thing and let an afternoon pass without touching it — no re-reading, no tuning, nothing added.
cells.core:
You can spot what matters before you know why, and instead of arriving, you stop at the examining — one more read, one more pass, deciding again what's already decided. What you tended with your own care has grown and finished, and you keep calling it provisional.

The direction is picked. What's left is the enjoying. Find something near you that you tended and that grew, say what it is, and give it one unhurried minute. No next move, no quality check, nothing to fix. Rest there a moment, then carry on. The result holds whether you re-examine it or not.
cells.sheetLine: The harvest finished. You're still at the doorway you came in by.
cells.verb: to pick the light to steer by and steer by it
cells.place: where you know what matters before you know why

cells.tense: You're steering while saying you have no hand on the wheel.
cells.act: let resources flow to the person who needs them
cells.ask: Send someone what they actually need — a name, a hand, an open door — and don't announce where it came from.
cells.core:
People near you move on course, and if asked how, nobody names you. There's a decided direction moving through your circle — some of it was chosen — and the one who chose it calls it obvious. Steer by a light this steadily and it stops looking like a light at all; it just looks like the way things are.

What you have is that steady, and it's made to go outward. Pick one person and one concrete thing you can hand them — a name, a piece of your time, a tool they need — and complete it before you take on anything else. Then notice what remains once it's handed over. That part is yours, and it was yours the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: Others travel by your course. You say you're not steering.

attempts.check: The claim the record doesn't back: that the person was once pulled and has since stopped — only the mechanism (past-anchored) and the seat's readiness imply it, never the person's history or what caused it. The reader could reasonably say no, I'm still very much being pulled, I just can't get moving tonight. Ask survives being wrong because skipping the arranging before a move is one small omission, not a verdict on their direction; if they skipped it and nothing was clarified, the omission cost them nothing and taught them nothing harmful. The sentence that serves me more than them: any line turning 'the harvest finished' into 'you finished it long ago and the fire went out' — that's my arc, not their record.
